Hi Helen — great to meet you and happy to outline options. Attached is a short proposal (BioCity_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a capacity matrix that maps workload profiles to cluster templates. Summary here so procurement has a quick read: 

1) BASELINE: Small reserved lane
- Min GPUs: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs
- Target throughput: steady-state ~3.5k token/sec (mixed workloads)
- Burst: +50% via warm burst pool (shared across customers)
- Typical commercial fit: early production or low-cost ML inference
- Tradeoffs: lower unit cost, limited parallel concurrent sessions

2) STANDARD: Production reserved cluster
- Min GPUs: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (3 x 8-GPU racks logical)
- Target throughput: ~10–12k token/sec with KV cache enabled for chat loads
- Burst: +100% using pre-warmed dedicated burst lanes for agreed ramp windows
- SLA: 99.9% latency SLO, priority routing, can pin models
- Commercial fit: most enterprise OLTP+batch mixed workloads

3) STEPPED ENTERPRISE: Phased ramp (recommended for growth deals)
- Initial min GPUs: 16; ramp to 64 over 6–9 months in three tranches (16 → 32 → 64)
- Warm start credits and reserved burst buckets during tranche transitions
- Autoscaling runway: we maintain warm instances and preloaded KV caches for pinned model variants
- Pricing: blended reserved rate + overage pricing for unplanned burst

Notes on technical levers: automatic KV/prefix cache, dynamic batching windows, and per-route model quantization profiles — these reduce effective GPU needs by up to ~30% on chat-heavy workloads. The attached matrix has estimated effective throughput with/without caching.

Next steps: Priyom will share a short technical note on padding/batching assumptions and recommended min GPUs for your 2–4k token context scenarios. Grace will coordinate the commercial terms and the ramp cadence options. Happy to jump on a call with Procurement next week.

Regards,
Karthik

Hi — quick technical clarifications from our side: 

• Floor flexibility: we can support a temporary reduced floor (20 GPUs) for months 1–3 under a 12‑month commitment if you accept a short warm-start credit allocation and a one-time configuration fee to pre-warm the reserved KV caches. This ensures latency targets while traffic ramps.

• Ramp triggers: we normally use a combination of sustained token/sec (rolling 72-hour average), 95th/99th latency percentiles, and a model-usage heatmap (pinned model hit rate > 70%) as automated thresholds. Example: move to next tranche when sustained throughput ≥ 80% of tranche capacity and 95th percentile latency < agreed SLO for 72 hours. We'll document the exact alert rules in the SLO appendix.

• Warm pool: dedicated burst lanes for enterprise customers are logically isolated (no shared customer model state). They still run on multi-tenant physical hosts in the same tenancy; we provide strict access controls and audit logs. For full physical isolation we can offer an HSM-backed private pool (additional cost).

• GPU classes: standard A100-equivalent for the quoted pricing. H100 hybrid upgrade available with ~+22% price increase and ~15–25% latency improvement on certain transformer kernels — we can model this for your largest models.

Example ramp schedule (we can adjust):
- Month 0 (post-sign): 20 GPUs active (warm pre-warm), 6k token/sec effective with heavy caching
- Month 2: 32 GPUs — target 9–11k token/sec, enable burst lanes
- Month 5: 48 GPUs — target 14–18k token/sec, full production

I attached a short Excel with the math. Happy to run a quick model-specific run-rate if you share a sample week of request sizes.

— Priyom
Senior Solution Engineer | Redwood Inference
